title: Brewers reach World Series after 44 years as Misierowski fans five and Yelich drives early run - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Brewers reach World Series after 44 years as Misierowski fans five and Yelich drives early run - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 24일(토) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Brewers reach World Series after 44 years as Misierowski fans five and Yelich drives early run 
 입력 2026.10.24. 12:40 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 The Milwaukee Brewers, returning to the World Series for the first time in 44 years and vying for the franchise's first championship, opened with a victory.
 Milwaukee defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 in Game 1 of the World Series on the 24th (Korean time) at American Family Field in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
 Tampa Bay set a starting lineup of Yandy Díaz (designated hitter), Jonathan Aranda (first base), Chandler Simpson (left field), Junior Caminero (third base), Liam Hicks (catcher), Jonny Deluca (center field), Victor Mesa Jr., Ben Williamson (second base) and Taylor Wols (shortstop). The starting pitcher was Nick Martinez.
 Milwaukee's starting lineup included Jackson Chourio (left field), Jake Bauers (first base), Christian Yelich (designated hitter), William Contreras (catcher), Bryce Turang (second base), Garrett Mitchell (center field), Cooper Pratt (shortstop), Sal Frelick (right field) and David Hamilton (third base). Jacob Misiorowski started on the mound.
 Milwaukee, which earned home-field advantage with 103 regular-season wins and the highest winning percentage in Major League Baseball, scored first in the first inning and seized control.
 Tampa Bay had the first opportunity. In the top of the first, after one out, Jonathan Aranda's single to right and Chandler Simpson's mis-hit to left created a one-out, runners on first and second chance, but Junior Caminero's ground ball to third prevented the runner on second from returning, resulting in a double play that ended the inning.
 In the bottom of the first, Milwaukee did not miss its chance. Leadoff Jackson Chourio's single to right created a one-out, runner on first opportunity, and Christian Yelich delivered an RBI triple to deep center to score the first run. William Contreras's single to left then made it 2-0.
 In the top of the fourth, Tampa Bay created a chance when Jonathan Aranda drew a walk and Junior Caminero hit a double over the center fielder's head to put runners on second and third with one out, and Liam Hicks's groundout to first cut the deficit by one.
 Neither team could add to the scoreboard. Tampa Bay suffered consecutive caught stealing attempts in scoring opportunities. In the top of the fifth with two outs and a runner on second, Victor Mesa Jr. was thrown out trying to steal third, and in the top of the sixth with one out and a runner on first, Jonathan Aranda was thrown out trying to steal second. Milwaukee catcher William Contreras contained Tampa Bay's speed.
 Milwaukee's starter Jacob Misiorowski left after pitching 5 innings, allowing 4 hits, 1 walk, striking out 3 and giving up 1 run, and Milwaukee added an insurance run in the bottom of the seventh. With two outs and runners on second and third after Cooper Pratt's walk and David Hamilton's shortstop groundout produced a 2-out, runner on second situation, Jackson Chourio's single to right extended the lead to 3-1.
 After Misiorowski, Abner Uribe worked 1 1/3 innings allowing 1 hit with 2 strikeouts and no runs, and Aaron Ashby followed with 1 2/3 innings, striking out 3 with no runs to close out the game PerfecT.
 Tampa Bay had one last chance in the top of the ninth. After one out, Jonathan Aranda's single to left, Chandler Simpson's single to center, a double steal, and Junior Caminero's walk loaded the bases with one out. Liam Hicks hit a grounder to second and it appeared the game would end on a double play, but the out at second was overturned to safe when shortstop Cooper Pratt's foot left the bag. Tampa Bay scored one run.
 In the ninth, Trevor Megill nearly created a bases-loaded crisis and allowed a run, but Milwaukee closed the game when Jonny Deluca struck out looking with two outs and runners on second and third in the bottom of the ninth.
